o1.biggest_strength: Nails our voice and principles with zero buzzwords, and turns our data into a clear, honest post and practical scorecard.
o1.biggest_mistake: The scorecard's 1/3/5 anchors are under the job post but the weights are on the scorecard; the post and scorecard are fine, but the application plan has the biggest leverage and should be more prominent.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the application plan with a projected hour count and a short note on how to calibrate reviewers; make the scorecard weights visually tie to the data table.

o2.biggest_strength: Provides a time-zone table and a concrete application-hour projection; thinks beyond the post with a bolder move to contact strong applicants later.
o2.biggest_mistake: Scorecard weights split writing into two 25/30% rows, but the interview rows total 45% and are only assessed in interviews, which may reintroduce interview impression bias.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Simplify the scorecard to keep writing dominant (e.g., 50% writing) and move interview-based rows to fewer, sharper weights; make the post's voice even more candid and less corporate.

reason: Output 2 makes the time-zone gap tangible with a local-hours table and shows exactly how the application plan saves reviewer hours, which an owner would appreciate. Its small voice lapses and scorecard weighting quirks keep the win narrow.
